newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* Goodyear Tire and the United Steelworkers union representing its workers have reached a tentative pact to end a two-week strike but the deal still needs ratification.
* An Italian merger deal which would have formed one of the world's biggest clothing conglomerates and joined some holdings of the prominent Marzotto and Agnelli families has been called off.

* Critics are upset the broadcast television industry is resisting attempts by President Clinton and campaign finance reformers to offer free public interest television air time to political candidates.
* Personal computer maker Compaq this month will launch plans to lower costs by changing the way its makes and distributes machines.
* "Married with Children," a television series by News Corp's Fox network is being retired after 11 years, after spawning a number of imitators.
* Metricom plans to introduce a second generation of its equipment which would offer data speeds near those of high-speed access lines by next year.
* Simon & Schuster took steps to recall thousands of copies of a book for junior high school students which portrayed Islam founder Muhammad as a cruel man.
* Advertising agency Cordiant said it named an outside marketing executive to take over its Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising Worldwide unit.
* Conde Nast Sports for Women publisher Deanna Brown has been replaced by Suzanne Grimes, publisher of TV Guide.
* Digital Commerce: Ticketmaster's suit against Microsoft, in which Microsoft is accused of allegedly diluting Ticketmaster's trademarks on the Web, could have broader implications for the Internet.
* Myriad Genetics is working on a test for a gene which could cause skin cancer melanoma.
* The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation said evidence from an investigation into the cause of the crash of Trans World Airlines flight 800 indicated a "catastrophic mechanical failure."

* A man paralyzed by a fall off a power pole in 1962 is still trying to obtain workers' compensation benefits. Utilities Mutual Insurance Co, the workers' compensation insurer for the man's former employer, Niagra Mohawk Power Corp, says it has no obligation to pay until appeals are over.
* Major cable companies are putting in orders for digital equipment which will enable them to expand their programming offerings but they are not making plans to provide high-definition programming.
* Post production film work including editing, scoring, sound mixing and digital effects are essential to produce a polished movie.
